summary: x402 is an agent payment helper that pays for HTTP resources with USDC on Base (chain ID 8453) or Base Sepolia by signing EIP-3009 transferWithAuthorization payloads and retrying requests with an X-Payment header. It requires a wallet private key, supplied via the PRIVATE_KEY or WALLET_PATH environment variables or an account object, and Node.js with the viem dependency. It contacts paid resource URLs and, in its example, api.conway.tech, and scans base64/JSON payment requirements from remote servers. No hosts or binaries beyond Node.js plus viem are needed; the metadata declares no environment variables even though the usage, examples and test script all read PRIVATE_KEY or WALLET_PATH.

findings.message: The usage example reads process.env.PRIVATE_KEY, an environment variable that metadata.openclaw.requires.env does not declare.
The documented Conway credits command sets PRIVATE_KEY on the shell command line, another key the release does not declare in requires.env.
loadWallet() reads process.env.PRIVATE_KEY to build the signing account, but requires.env declares nothing.
loadWallet() also reads process.env.WALLET_PATH to locate a wallet file, an undeclared environment variable.
The private key from process.env.PRIVATE_KEY is passed to privateKeyToAccount, handling a raw wallet credential.
wallet.privateKey read from the WALLET_PATH JSON file is passed to privateKeyToAccount, consuming a private key from disk.
Prerequisites state an Ethereum wallet with private key is required, revealing the skill depends on a private key credential.
Builds a URL at api.conway.tech embedding the wallet address and top-up amount, then pays it via x402Fetch, sending data to that host.
x402Fetch issues an HTTP request to the caller-supplied url, which may be any remote host.
After payment the signed X-Payment authorization is resent to the same remote URL, exposing the signature to that host.
The npm test script runs node examples/conway-credits.mjs, so running tests executes payment code that requires wallet credentials.
The skill card cites only server release metadata and package.json for version 1.0.0 while the SKILL.md advertises conway-domain.mjs, which is absent from the release.
